name: Autosomal Dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2I

ethnicAssociations: Reported in multiple ethnic groups without specific predilection

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for CMT2I

criteria.description: Presence of distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting lower limbs
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy with normal or mildly reduced nerve conduction velocities
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the GARS gene
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Distal sensory loss and impaired proprioception

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of distal motor neuropathy symptoms, electrophysiological confirmation of axonal neuropathy, and identification of a pathogenic GARS mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical presentation may overlap with other CMT subtypes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness and atrophy of lower limbs
Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes in lower limbs
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy with normal or mildly reduced conduction velocities
searchTerms: nerve damage with mostly normal conduction speed
nerve tests showing axon loss but near normal speed

common.symptomName: Distal sensory loss including impaired vibration and proprioception
searchTerms: loss of vibration and position sense in hands and feet

common.symptomName: Steppage gait due to foot drop
searchTerms: steppage gait due to foot drop

common.symptomName: Mild hand muscle weakness and atrophy
searchTerms: slight weakness and muscle loss in hands

common.symptomName: Numbness and paresthesia in distal extremities
searchTerms: numbness and tingling in hands and feet
abnormal feelings in fingers and toes
muscle cramps in hands and feet

rare.symptomName: Respiratory muscle involvement leading to mild dyspnea
searchTerms: difficulty breathing due to weak breathing muscles
shortness of breath from respiratory muscle weakness

rare.symptomName: Cranial nerve involvement causing facial weakness

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of neuropathy
imaging: MRI may show muscle atrophy in distal limbs
Spinal imaging to assess for scoliosis if present
other: Nerve conduction studies showing axonal neuropathy pattern

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent motor involvement with earlier onset
Inflammatory etiology with demyelinating features on nerve conduction studies

references: Rossor AM, Polke JM, Houlden H, Reilly MM. Clinical implications of genetic advances in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Nat Rev Neurol. 2013;9(10):562-571.
Orphanet: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2I. ORPHA:99942.
